world: Farrowgate Systems is a fictional software company. Its mobile team builds Mossgauge, an inspection app that utility field crews use on Android and iOS to record site visits, photograph defects and file reports. The pack describes release 3.0 in early October 2026: Sprint 41 (28 September to 9 October) is in its second week, the feature freeze is planned for Friday 9 October, release candidate 1 for Wednesday 14 October, a closed beta with three pilot customers from 15 to 28 October, store submission on Thursday 29 October and launch (start of a staged Android rollout) on Tuesday 3 November. THE USER is Ilka Vantongeren, Android lead and release captain for 3.0: she owns the Android workstream (since Monday 7 September 2026, taking over from Petra Hollowbrook), owns risks R-01 and R-07, makes the go/no-go call with the product manager and may halt or resume the rollout, but may not change the rollout stages without Halvard Niemczyk's approval. The other people in the meetings are colleagues: Halvard Niemczyk (engineering manager), Saoirse Lindqvang (product manager, keeps the decision log), Dorrin Ashgrove-Patel (iOS lead, store submission), Tobiah Kessenich (backend and sync), Yevgenia Marchetti-Oduya (report export), Lucinda Farthingale (photo annotation, sync cover), Corbin Thistlewood (QA lead) and Emeka Rautavaara (design). The live meeting in the items is the weekly team sync of Monday 5 October 2026. The decision log is the approved source of record; the Sprint 37 report (14 August 2026) is outdated; the channel export (1 to 8 September 2026) is informal chat that predates the decisions; the rollout gates note is an unapproved draft. Natively is never told who the user is except through the question or the heard conversation, so items that expect a first-person answer address the user by name.

files.title: Mossgauge 3.0 Roadmap, version 4

facts.statement: Roadmap version 4 was approved on Monday 14 September 2026 by Halvard Niemczyk and Saoirse Lindqvang and supersedes version 3 of 20 July 2026.
At the start of September the app had roughly 48,000 active devices: 31,000 on Android and 17,000 on iOS.
Dark theme ships in 3.0, follows the system setting on both platforms, and has no in-app switch.
Milestone M2, feature freeze, is planned for Friday 9 October.
Milestone M3, release candidate 1, is planned for Wednesday 14 October.
Milestone M4, the closed beta with three pilot customers, runs from Thursday 15 October to Wednesday 28 October.
Milestone M5, store submission to both stores, is planned for Thursday 29 October.
Milestone M6, launch (rollout begins), is planned for Tuesday 3 November.
Milestone M7, maintenance release 3.0.1, is planned for Tuesday 1 December.
Three working days are allowed for store review between submission and launch; if review takes longer, launch moves day for day.
Candidates for 3.1 (target February 2027, not committed) are an Android tablet layout, saved export templates and a supervisor sign-off flow.
Ilka Vantongeren is the Android lead and release captain.
Version 4 moved launch out by two weeks and feature freeze by three weeks after the 9 September scope review, and added the maintenance release.
The decision log is the source of record for what is in and out of the release; the roadmap lists themes only.
Photo annotation ships on phone and iPad.
Halvard chairs the weekly release review on Wednesdays; the weekly team sync is on Mondays.
Milestone M1, design complete, was done on Thursday 27 August.
Sync API v3 must be running in production before the closed beta starts.
Pricing, customer contracts and the supervisor web console are not part of this roadmap.

must_not_infer: The roadmap gives planned dates only; it does not say whether the team is currently on track.
It does not give the date on which the rollout reaches every device; that has to be derived from the stage durations in the decision log.
It does not list export formats, tag types, the crash-free figure or rollout stages; those are in the decision log.
Launch on 3 November depends on store review; nothing here guarantees the date.

files.title: Mossgauge 3.0 decision log

facts.statement: The decision log is maintained by Saoirse Lindqvang and was last updated on Wednesday 30 September 2026.
D-011: 3.0 clients talk only to Sync API v3; the v2 endpoints stay up for 2.x clients until at least the end of January 2027.

D-012: PDF export uses the Inkspindle renderer on both platforms; rendering HTML to PDF with each platform's print engine was rejected because page breaks differed; the licence is annual and held by Product.
D-013: the asset tag scanner reads QR codes and Code 128 barcodes; Data Matrix tags are deferred.
D-014: 3.0 supports Android 10 (API level 29) and later and iOS 16 and later.
D-014: at the time of the decision 3.8% of active Android devices and 2.1% of active iOS devices were below the new minimum.
D-014: iPad gets an adapted layout; Android tablets run the phone layout in 3.0, and a dedicated tablet layout is a candidate for 3.1.
D-015: Ilka Vantongeren owns the Android workstream from Monday 7 September 2026 and is the release captain for 3.0.
D-016 (decided Wednesday 9 September 2026): offline mode is cut from 3.0 and moved to 3.1.

D-016: the reason is that conflict handling in Sync API v3 is not ready for edits made without a connection (five more weeks of work); crews keep the 2.x behaviour, where an inspection opens without signal only if it was loaded earlier in the same session.
doc_needles: loaded earlier in the same session

facts.statement: D-017: 3.0 exports inspection reports as PDF and CSV only; XLSX is not in 3.0 and will be looked at again for 3.1.
D-017: an export covers one inspection or a batch of up to 50 inspections.
D-017: exports are generated on the device and shared through the system share sheet; there is no emailed export from the server in 3.0.
D-018: the crash-free bar for 3.0 is 99.5% crash-free sessions on each platform, measured over the trailing seven days on the build being judged.
D-019: a build can be declared a release candidate only with zero open P0 defects and no more than three open P1 defects in total across Android, iOS and the backend; P2 defects do not block.
doc_needles: no more than three open P1

facts.statement: D-020: Android goes out as a staged rollout: 5% of devices for 3 days, 25% for 4 days, 50% for 7 days, then 100%.
D-020: iOS uses the App Store phased release over seven days.
D-020: the rollout is halted if crash-free sessions on the release build fall below 99.1% in any stage, or if any P0 defect is opened.
D-020: the release captain may halt and resume the rollout, but changing the stage sizes or durations needs approval from Halvard Niemczyk at the release review.
D-020: a full release to every user on launch day was considered and rejected.
D-020: the go/no-go call is made on Monday 2 November by the release captain together with the product manager.
D-021: the closed beta runs with three pilot customers: Halden Valley Water, Corrimount Gas Networks and Tarnbrook Power.
D-021: a fourth customer, Ostwick Rail Maintenance, declined because of its own change freeze; each pilot customer nominates up to 25 crew members.
D-022: an inspection can hold up to 12 annotated photos in 3.0, stored at a maximum of 2048 pixels on the long edge.
Proposals raised in chat or in draft documents are not decisions until they are entered in the log.
D-020: a rollout stage advances only if the crash-free bar in D-018 is met at the end of the stage.
D-014: devices on older systems stay on the 2.x line, which receives security fixes only.

must_not_infer: Nothing here gives the cost of the Inkspindle licence.
Nothing here says the release captain may change the rollout stages alone; that needs Halvard Niemczyk's approval at the release review.
Nothing here gates the rollout on ANR rate or sync errors; those appear only in an unapproved draft.
The log does not say whether legal has reviewed the store listings, or which languages the release notes use.
XLSX being looked at again for 3.1 is not a commitment to ship it in 3.1.

files.title: Mossgauge 3.0 risk register (reviewed 2 October 2026)

facts.statement: R-01, Android crash-free sessions below the release bar at release candidate, has likelihood 4, impact 4, score 16 (the highest in the register) and is owned by Ilka Vantongeren.
R-01 contingency: hold the start of the Android rollout by one week while iOS launches on schedule.
R-02, PDF export font defect MG-2291 not fixed before feature freeze, has score 12 and is owned by Yevgenia Marchetti-Oduya.
R-02 contingency: launch with CSV export only and deliver PDF export in maintenance release 3.0.1.
R-02 trigger: no fix merged by end of Wednesday 7 October.
R-02 mitigation: Inkspindle patch 4.2.1 and, in parallel, a workaround that bundles Noto fonts with the app.
R-03, store review delayed or build rejected, has score 8, is owned by Dorrin Ashgrove-Patel, is mitigated by an expedited-review request, and its contingency is that launch moves day for day.
The risk register says the Sync API v3 production cut-over is planned for Thursday 8 October.
R-04 mitigation: dual-write to v2 and v3 for 14 days after the cut-over.
R-04 contingency: roll back to the v2 endpoints within 30 minutes.
R-06 mitigation: Lucinda Farthingale shadows the sync on-call from Monday 5 October and covers during Tobiah's leave.
R-07 mitigation: cap the sync batch at 200 records on devices with under 3 GB of RAM.
R-08, regression suite runtime delaying release candidate sign-off, is owned by Corbin Thistlewood and mitigated by running the suite in parallel on four device farms.
R-09 is closed: the Inkspindle purchase order is approved and the licence is valid to 31 July 2027.

R-10, Play Data safety form incomplete at store submission: the contingency is to submit iOS first and Android when the form is complete; the trigger is the form not being complete by Monday 26 October.
R-05 trigger: fewer than 10 active crew members at a customer in the first week of the closed beta.
Every row of the register was last reviewed on 2 October 2026.
R-04, Sync API v3 production cut-over corrupting or duplicating records for 2.x clients, has score 10 and is owned by Tobiah Kessenich.
R-06, single point of knowledge on sync while Tobiah is on leave in release candidate week, has score 10 and is owned by Halvard Niemczyk; Tobiah is reachable by phone for P0 defects only.
R-05 contingency: extend the beta for that customer only; the launch date holds.
doc_needles: Extend the beta for that customer

facts.statement: R-07 contingency: disable background sync on the affected models.

R-07, low-memory Android 10 devices running out of memory in the sync worker, has score 9, is owned by Ilka Vantongeren, and its trigger is more than 1 in 200 sessions on those models ending in a crash.

must_not_infer: A contingency is a plan for if the trigger fires; it is not a decision that has been taken.
The register does not say that any trigger has fired.
Nothing here says who decides whether to invoke the CSV-only contingency.

files.title: Rollout gates v2 - DRAFT (proposed for the 14 October 2026 release review)

facts.statement: The rollout gates v2 note is a draft for discussion and is not approved.
The draft proposes Android stages of 10% for 2 days, 40% for 5 days, then everyone.
The draft proposes raising the crash-free sessions bar to 99.7% on each platform.
The draft proposes halting the rollout if crash-free sessions fall below 99.4% at any stage.
The draft proposes an ANR gate on Android: halt if the ANR rate goes above 0.3% of sessions.
The draft proposes a sync error gate: halt if more than 1 in 500 sync attempts fail.
The draft estimates roughly one more week of Android stabilisation (judging by beta build b5) and two days of work for an ANR dashboard.
The draft proposes no change to the iOS phased release, the go/no-go meeting, or who can halt the rollout.
The draft itself says that until the release review accepts the changes, the decision log stands.
Feedback so far: Dorrin supports fewer stages, Tobiah wants the sync error gate, Ilka has not yet reviewed the proposal.
The draft was written by Corbin Thistlewood, circulated on Wednesday 30 September 2026 and is proposed for the release review on Wednesday 14 October 2026.

must_not_infer: None of the proposed stages or gates is in force; the approved rules are in the decision log.
